newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian singer Fela sues drug agency over arrest.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian singer Fela sues drug agency over arrest.

text.p: Maverick musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti on Monday filed a suit at a Lagos court against Nigeria's anti-narcotics agency for his "unlawful arrest and detention", his lawyer said.
Femi Falana said Fela was claiming 100 million naira ($1.2 million) in damages from the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) for alleged violation of his human rights.

NDLEA officials stormed Fela's home and nightclub called "The Shrine" in Ikeja, a working class district in Lagos, last week and arrested the singer and 107 people for allegedly possessing large quantities of marijuana.

Falana, himself a fierce critic of the Nigerian military authorities, said Fela also wanted the court to ask NDLEA officers to vacate "The Shrine". The suit named Major-General Musa Bamaiyi, who commands NDLEA.
Those arrested have been detained at NDLEA headquarters Bamaiyi said at a news conference last Friday that after investigation action which he did not specity would be taken against them.
He said his agency had tried to give Fela counselling for his drug habit.
At the same news conference, Fela who was handcuffed said what he smoked was "grass" and not drugs.
"I have been smoking for 40 years. It helps my music. People know I smoke worldwide. It is not drugs, it is grass," he said.
Afro-beat superstar Fela, 58, is no stranger to controversy -- or to the jail cell. He has a reputation for openly smoking marijuana and dressing only in his underpants.
Fela was in the past critical of Nigeria's military rulers, but recently he has been a recluse at "The Shrine", occasionally performing in musical shows.
